claims: The Artemis 2 mission is estimated to cost approximately $4.1 billion for a single launch, according to a 2021 audit by NASA's Office of Inspector General.
The approximately $4.1 billion expense for the Artemis 2 mission covers the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
The approximately $4.1 billion expense for the Artemis 2 mission covers the Orion capsule.
Total spending for the entire Artemis program through 2025 is projected at roughly $93 billion.
The high cost of the Artemis program is largely due to the development of the SLS rocket.
The high cost of the Artemis program is largely due to the development of the Orion capsule.
Multiple sources estimate the cost per launch for Artemis I through IV to be between $4 billion and $4.2 billion.
The overall Artemis program is estimated to cost over $90 billion through 2025.
The overall Artemis program is aimed at returning humans to the Moon.
The overall Artemis program is aimed at establishing a long-term presence.
The Artemis program is primarily funded by U.S. taxpayers.
The Artemis program receives additional support from international partners such as the European Space Agency (ESA).
